column1: # OUTSIDE_SPITBOL_BASELINE.tsv -- gimpel: the 28 drivers the ONE ORACLE does not answer, so they are OUTSIDE
# the graded baseline and OUT OF THE DENOMINATOR (116 scored of 144 shipped). Lon 2026-09-08: the leaderboard
# divides by the programs SPITBOL runs clean, and a program SPITBOL cannot run is recorded per program with
# SPITBOL's own error AND a source check. Written coo 2026-09-08; test_snoflake_suite.sh is the shape.
# MEASURED LIVE 2026-09-08 with /home/resources/x64/bin/sbl -bf, each driver in a staged copy of the package.
# The runner's own UNSCR arm decides this set each run and cross-checks it against this file.
# ⛔ THIS FILE IS NOT MIRRORED ROW FOR ROW BY UNGRADABLE.tsv HERE, AND MUST NOT BE. In the other packages the
# two files hold the same set, so the mirror keeps the inventory summing. Gimpel is shaped differently:
# UNGRADABLE.tsv holds 174 rows -- the 146 vendored LIBRARY sources that are not programs at all, plus these
# 28 drivers -- and shipped 290 = graded 116 + ungradable 174 balances. Every row below was verified present
# there. Adding them again would double-count them and break the sum. THE RECORD AND THE BUCKET ARE NOT THE
# SAME SET IN EVERY PACKAGE; check before mirroring.
# ⭐ THE 28 ARE NOT ONE THING, AND FLATTENING THEM WOULD HIDE THE MOST USEFUL FACT IN THE SET: SEVEN drivers
# fail at THE SAME LINE OF THE SAME INCLUDED FILE, BAL.sno(11), and THREE more at REDEFINE.sno(17). Those are
# two shared library sources, not ten independent programs -- if either is ever brought inside the baseline it
# moves seven and three entries at once. ⛔ THE COUNTS IN THIS PARAGRAPH SAID five AND two WHEN THE FILE HELD
# 17 ROWS, AND BOTH WERE UNDERCOUNTS FOR THE SAME REASON THE 11 BELOW WERE MISSING: GPM and PEEL die at
# BAL.sno(11) and INFINIP_lib at REDEFINE.sno(17), and all three were being graded RED against a pin instead
# of counted here. A shared-library group is exactly the fact a per-file census cannot see; count it, never
# carry it forward.
# ⛔⭐ THE ELEVEN ROWS AT THE BOTTOM WERE ADDED 2026-09-08 (hq_B) AND THEY ARE THE INTERESTING HALF OF THIS
# FILE'S HISTORY. They were not a new measurement -- the package's OWN ALL.excluded.txt already named all 28
# drivers "oracle died: graceful fatal report -- no ground truth to grade against". Seventeen of the 28 had no
# .ref and reached this file. The other ELEVEN carried a .ref that the 2026-09-07 recut (corpus fd77d6e45)
# wrote FROM THAT VERY FATAL REPORT, so scorecard_snobol4.sh's run_one saw have_pin=1, never consulted its own
# sbl_died liveness guard (which it applies only to the LIVE oracle run, never to a pin), and graded SCRIP
# against SPITBOL's death dump -- eleven permanent reds. ⭐ THE DISCRIMINATOR BETWEEN THE TWO TREATMENTS WAS
# NOT THE ORACLE'S ANSWER BUT WHETHER A PIN FILE HAPPENED TO EXIST: FTRACE_driver above and TRIG_driver below
# draw the IDENTICAL ERROR 248 from the identical cause, and one was outside the baseline while the other was
# a red. ⛔ AND THEY WERE UNWINNABLE ON THEIR FACE: a matching run would have had to reproduce SPITBOL's
# termination block, including its own heap accounting ("memory used (bytes) 15640", "memory left (bytes)
# 1032928"). NOBODY COULD HAVE PASSED THEM. The eleven pins are deleted; ALL.excluded.txt is the record of
# why they must never be re-minted.
# ⛔ AND THE LAST TWO ARE A DIFFERENT KIND OF FACT ENTIRELY. TIMEGC and TIMER do not fail on SNOBOL4 the oracle
# dislikes; they fail because an include they name IS NOT IN THE CORPUS. resolution.sno does not exist anywhere
# under corpus/ at all, and system.inc exists only at corpus/programs/lon_cherryholmes/include/system.inc,
# outside this package. That is OUR packaging gap, not SPITBOL's refusal, and it is recorded as
# ORACLE_CONTRACT_NOT_IMPLEMENTED rather than ORACLE_REFUSES so nobody reads it as a language question.
# system.inc could be vendored; resolution.sno cannot be, because we do not have it.
# Columns: name <TAB> CLASS <TAB> does not run in SPITBOL: <error, file(line)>; source checked <date> (<who>): <why>
